claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2025-11-18 and 2026-08-27, Administration placed at least two distinct proposals to change Edmonton snow and ice control service on a published City Council or Council committee agenda, and each proposal stated new spending to deliver it.
claims.interpretation_notes: Primary count: P=3, C=3, U=0; Supported. I count the November 2025 parking-ban towing and active-pathway packages, plus the Well Maintained City package listed for the 2026-08-31 committee meeting. I group the 24 dependent enhancements in CO03513 Attachment 10 with that presentation under the primary package unit; they are separately costed options under the alternative unit. I exclude the November 2025 Winter/Summer Temporary Assignment package: it changes employment status across several services but specifies no change to snow and ice control service or operations. The 2026-08-31 agenda's reported 2026-08-22 archive capture is the basis for counting Well Maintained City by the comment date; I could not independently retrieve that capture. Required alternatives, changing only the named rule: considered by a body by 2026-08-27, P=2/C=2/U=0, Supported; window through 2026-10-02, P=3/C=3/U=0, Supported; start at 2025-01-01, P=3/C=3/U=0 after deduplicating the earlier versions of the two Fall 2025 packages, Supported; City Council alone, P=2/C=2/U=0, Supported; separately costed options, P=27/C=27/U=0 if all 24 items in Attachment 10 are treated as snow and ice enhancements, Supported; cost exceeding an explicitly identified approved budget, P=3/C=0/U=0, Contradicted because none of the three counted package texts gives both an approved snow-service budget figure and its increase against that figure; exactly two, P=3/C=3/U=0, Partially supported because a third costed package is listed. The stricter cost and exact-count readings change the rung. 'Already asked' here means placed on a published agenda: the Well Maintained City item was not considered by the committee until 2026-08-31. Neither placement nor consideration establishes approval or expenditure.

supporting_evidence.finding: The 2025-11-24 City Council agenda lists report FCS03158 and Attachment 2 under item 7.2; the 2025-12-01 budget agenda lists them again under item 5.2.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The Fall 2025 budget documents were placed before City Council within the primary reference period.

supporting_evidence.finding: Attachment 2, DocumentId 278877, pages 34 and 43–44, presents two distinct unfunded packages: parking-ban towing for CAD $100,000 ongoing in 2026, and improved active-pathway snow removal and sidewalk repair with CAD $9.938 million in new 2026 operating budget and CAD $2.11 million in one-time capital investment stated in its description.
supporting_evidence.source_title: FCS03158 Attachment 2, Fall 2025 Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment
supporting_evidence.establishes: At least two separately presented packages propose changes connected to snow clearing and state new spending. The integrated package's operating figures conflict internally and require qualification.

supporting_evidence.finding: The parking-ban package says contracted towing would remove some vehicles before blading and states CAD $100,000 of new ongoing budget in 2026.
supporting_evidence.source_title: FCS03158 Attachment 2, parking-ban enforcement package, page 34
supporting_evidence.establishes: The package changes a snow-clearing support operation and meets the primary cost reading.
supporting_evidence.quote: improves service levels for snow and ice control

supporting_evidence.finding: The active-pathway package states CAD $1.60 million annually for snow and ice control, CAD $1.64 million for enforcement and CAD $4.59 million for sidewalk repair; its table instead shows CAD $9.938 million in total new 2026 operating budget.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The package expressly changes active-pathway snow clearing and states incremental spending, though its total cost is inconsistent across sections.

supporting_evidence.finding: The 2026-08-31 Community and Public Services Committee agenda lists CO03513, DocumentId 304803, and Attachment 9, DocumentId 304812, under item 7.1. The brief identifies an archive capture dated 2026-08-22, before the comment.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Community and Public Services Committee agenda, 2026-08-31
supporting_evidence.establishes: The live agenda lists the package. The pre-comment publication date rests on the archive metadata supplied in the brief, which I could not verify independently.

supporting_evidence.finding: CO03513 describes the Well Maintained City service package as approximately CAD $23.6 million in ongoing annual operating spending and CAD $11.5 million in one-time capital spending for seasonal services, including residential clearing and active pathways.
supporting_evidence.source_title: CO03513, Snow and Ice Control Policy and Program Review
supporting_evidence.establishes: A third package proposes changes to snow and ice control and states new spending. The figures cover a broader seasonal package, not snow clearing alone.

supporting_evidence.finding: Attachment 9 describes an eight-day residential clearing window when activated, a dedicated snow and ice team for major events, and a Priority 1 active-pathway crew, within the CAD $23.6 million annual operating and CAD $11.5 million one-time capital package.
supporting_evidence.source_title: CO03513 Attachment 9, Well Maintained City Package Summary
supporting_evidence.establishes: The proposed package contains concrete snow-service changes and a stated package cost.

challenging_evidence.finding: CO03513 says Well Maintained City is provided ahead of formal presentation during 2027–2030 budget deliberations; policy C409L itself needs no additional budget, and optional enhancements depend on future direction and funding.
challenging_evidence.source_title: CO03513, Snow and Ice Control Policy and Program Review
challenging_evidence.establishes: The package had been presented for information, not formally submitted for budget approval; the policy approval must not be counted as a spending approval.

challenging_evidence.finding: The committee minutes first record presentations, questions and motions under CO03513 on 2026-08-31, four days after the comment. E. Rutherford's policy recommendation carried 5–0; A. Knack withdrew a motion to bring Well Maintained City to Council on 2026-09-08; J. Morgan's assisted-snow package request and J. Wright's school-zone package request each carried 5–0.
challenging_evidence.source_title: Community and Public Services Committee minutes, 2026-08-31, item 7.1
challenging_evidence.establishes: Well Maintained City had not been considered by a body by 2026-08-27. The later motions requested future packages; they did not fund them.

challenging_evidence.finding: On 2026-09-08, Council approved policy C409L through the reports-not-selected-for-debate vote, moved by K. Tang and seconded by T. Parmar, 12–0. Item 7.9 records no vote funding the service packages.
challenging_evidence.establishes: Council approval of a policy cannot establish that Council approved the proposed new spending.

challenging_evidence.finding: The 2025-11-24 Council meeting considered the Fall budget items and postponed them to 2025-12-01. On 2025-12-01, Council approved the revised operating adjustment 11–2; the recorded operating amendments contain no vote funding either snow-related unfunded package.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The proposals were considered, but the consulted minutes do not show Council funding those two packages.

challenging_evidence.finding: The Winter/Summer Temporary Assignment package seeks CAD $1.777 million in 2026 to convert temporary assignments to permanent positions across several services, including snow and ice, but states no snow-specific service change.
challenging_evidence.source_title: FCS03158 Attachment 2, Winter/Summer Temporary Assignment package, pages 45–46
challenging_evidence.establishes: This costed workforce package should not inflate the primary snow-service proposal count without a stated change to that service.

limitations: The portal returned a browser check or HTTP 403 to my web tool. I used the complete carried text of CO03513, Attachments 9 and 10, FCS03158, its four selected Attachment 2 sections, CO03079 and Attachment 5, plus the selected meeting items. I could not independently compare the 2026-08-22 agenda capture with the live file versions.

The Internet Archive URL and digest supplied in the brief indicate that CO03513 was on the 2026-08-31 agenda by 2026-08-22, but the archive did not load in my tools. The exact first publication day is unverified; the count of two Fall 2025 costed packages, and thus the primary Supported verdict, does not depend on that third package.

The full 144-page FCS03158 Attachment 2 was not accessible. The carried section inventory and complete snow-related sections support the identified packages, but I could not independently search every page or verify whether DocumentIds 278877 and 280346 are byte-identical.

FCS03158 Attachment 2 disagrees internally on the active-pathway package's annual operating amount: its description gives CAD $7.83 million in components, while its summary and new-budget table give CAD $9.938 million for 2026. It also gives CAD $2.11 million one-time capital. No unstated reconciliation is assumed.

The selected meeting-page items are not whole pages, and I could not comprehensively inspect every Council and committee agenda in the portal calendar from 2025-01-01 through 2026-10-02. The exact proposal count, particularly under the pre-election and option-unit alternatives, is less secure than the finding that at least two qualify.
CO03513's CAD $23.6 million annual operating and CAD $11.5 million one-time capital figures cover a combined winter and complementary seasonal package; the report does not isolate a snow-only share.
unknowns: The exact date CO03513 item 7.1 and its attachments first appeared on a public agenda, beyond the supplied archive's 2026-08-22 capture date.

Whether the City has an itemized, approved 2026 snow and ice control budget baseline against which every proposal's increase can be measured. CO03079 reports a CAD $67 million annual snow and ice control budget for 2025, but the three counted package texts do not state an approved baseline and increase together.
Whether other relevant agendas in the defined windows contain additional distinct Administration packages.

missing_evidence.likely_holder: Internet Archive and City of Edmonton Office of the City Clerk

missing_evidence.description: Complete searchable agenda and report set for all Council and standing committee meetings in the defined windows, including publication timestamps and earlier versions.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Office of the City Clerk

missing_evidence.description: An approved, itemized snow and ice control budget baseline for each counted package, with the proposal's increase against that baseline.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Financial and Corporate Services and City Operations

calculations_needed: If reporting the active-pathway package total, reconcile CAD $1.60 million + CAD $1.64 million + CAD $4.59 million = CAD $7.83 million annual operating components against the separate CAD $9.938 million new-2026-budget table; do not silently choose one.

For a snow-only Well Maintained City cost, obtain an itemized allocation. Do not present its CAD $23.6 million annual operating and CAD $11.5 million one-time capital package totals as snow-only spending.
what_would_change_my_verdict: A complete, dated agenda record showing that fewer than two of the identified Fall 2025 packages were publicly listed by 2026-08-27, or complete package text showing one did not propose a snow-service change or new spending, would lower the primary verdict.
An additional clearly distinct, costed package would change the exact count and related alternatives, though the primary at-least-two verdict would remain Supported.
claims.suggested_one_line: Under the published-agenda rule, Administration had already placed at least two costed snow-service proposals before Council by 2026-08-27; the later Well Maintained City committee item raises the identified package count to three if its reported 2026-08-22 agenda capture is confirmed.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Supported. Two distinct costed packages were on City Council's Fall 2025 budget agenda: CAD $100,000 ongoing for parking-ban towing and an integrated active-pathway snow-clearing package with stated new spending. A third, Well Maintained City, was listed for the 2026-08-31 committee meeting in an agenda reported captured before the comment, but was not considered until that meeting. The stricter approved-budget-baseline and exactly-two readings produce different verdicts.
